title: Mr. D's Classroom OS — Persisted State
description: Schema for the app state stored in localStorage under key 'mrd-classroom-os-v1'. Mirrors the complete structure written by js/core/store.js defaultState().

activeCore.description: Currently active house core (1–4 or 'all' for dashboard view).

settings.description: Teacher-configurable settings (edited in Admin → ⚙️ Settings). A fresh install seeds every sub-object below (moduleThemes, layouts, combat, sfx, introVideos) with real, non-null objects straight from store.js's defaultState() — a null value only ever shows up in an OLDER SAVED state that predates one of these settings, and store.js's load() migration fills it in with the shipped default the next time that save is loaded, without disturbing anything the teacher already customised. The exception is 'diceProphecy', which is deliberately NOT a copy of anything: it holds only the teacher's per-outcome overrides, merged over the table that ships in store.js, so a shipped wording fix reaches an install that has already saved. See each field's own description below.

seasonal.description: Enable seasonal ambient effects (falling leaves, snow, etc.).

mapsApiKeyOverride.description: Teacher's own Google Maps API key (blank = use bundled default).

soundEnabled.description: Master switch for all sound effects and voice lines (Admin → Sound). Turning it off silences everything, regardless of what 'sfx' or 'ambient' below are individually set to.

quietMode.description: Quiet mode (Admin → 🎨 Look & Sound → Display & Theme). Mutes sound effects (forces soundEnabled off when turned on) and freezes ambient/seasonal animation, for test days or quiet work time. Absent on older saves — store.js's getQuietMode() reads it as falsy until the teacher turns it on, so no migration is needed.

ambient.description: Quiet per-screen background music loops (see js/core/ambient.js). Off by default — this is opt-in, and the teacher turns it on in Admin.

tracks.description: moduleId -> audio source for that screen's loop. null/missing falls back to CONFIG.AMBIENT_TRACKS' shipped defaults. Also holds one PSEUDO-SCREEN key, 'flyover' (see js/core/store.js's FLYOVER_TRACK_KEY): the music that plays under Place of the Week's Google Maps 3D flight. It rides in this same map so the teacher assigns it in Admin → Settings → Background music next to every other screen's track, but it is deliberately NOT a real module id — js/core/ambient.js only looks up tracks by the id of the module actually mounted, and no module is called 'flyover', so nothing plays it as an ordinary background loop by accident. js/modules/potw.js reads it directly instead. Flight music used to be set per POTW destination; it is now one global choice.

lock.description: Teacher PIN lock (js/core/lock.js), which can gate actions like using a Magic Shop item or overriding a Battle Day result.

pinHash.description: Hashed PIN. An empty string means the lock is OFF, which is the default — the app must never lock a teacher out of a fresh install.

len.description: Number of digits in the PIN, so the on-screen PIN pad knows when an entry is complete.

minutes.description: Minutes of inactivity after which the lock re-engages and a PIN is required again.

moduleThemes.description: Per-screen accent colour overrides (Admin → Appearance), for the three screens whose colour is actually configurable: 'dashboard' (Home screen), 'quests' (Quests board), and 'houses' (Records). Every other screen (Magic Shop, Battle Day, Dice, Council, POTW) has its palette baked into the CSS on purpose, so listing them here would show a control that does nothing. null in a state that predates this setting or has never been migrated; store.js load() seeds any screen the saved state has never seen with its shipped default, without disturbing a screen the teacher has already customised.

color.description: Hex accent colour for this screen, used when 'matchHouse' is false.

matchHouse.description: If true, ignore 'color' and follow the currently active house's own accent instead. The Home screen ships this as true so it always feels like 'your' house's dashboard; the Quests board ships it false on purpose — the house accents already cover red/blue/amber/green, and a quest board that borrows them would look like a different app every period.

layouts.description: Per-screen display mode for the two screens that support both a scrolling grid and a horizontal carousel: 'quests' and 'shop'. Grid (the default) suits scanning ~20 quests or items at a glance; carousel suits a teacher standing at a smartboard swiping through one card at a time instead of scrolling with a mouse. null in a state that predates this setting; store.js load() fills in 'grid' for any screen not yet set.

combatMode.description: Which of the TWO complete Battle Day rule sets is active (see store.js's COMBAT_MODES). 'duel' — "Mr. D's own rules" and the shipped default — is a dice-and-counters game: each house holds at most one attack item and one defense item at a time (see 'shop.catalog' items' 'slot'/'counteredBy'/'blocks'), an attack reveals the defender's held item and either is cancelled outright or rolls real dice on screen, and the total comes straight off the DEFENDER'S POINTS (never HP). 'hp' is the earlier hit-points model, kept fully working as an alternative: strikes remove hit points (top-level 'hp' key) rather than points, and only a battle's winner is paid a points prize (see 'combat' below) when the loser's HP reaches zero — the loser's points are never touched either way. store.setCombatMode() is the only way this is written; switching modes swaps 'shop.catalog' for the other mode's catalog (see 'shop.parked') and clears the top-level 'inventory' and 'hp' keys, because an item bought under one rule set means nothing under the other. It does NOT touch points, the transaction log, quests, the planner, or any other setting.

combat.description: Battle Day combat tuning (Admin → ⚔️ Battle Day / ⚙️ Settings → ⚔️ Battle rules). Seeded with real values by store.js's defaultState() on a brand-new install — it is never null there. A null/missing value only ever turns up in an OLDER SAVED state from before this setting existed; store.js load() merges that over store.defaultCombat()'s defaults the next time it loads. store.updateCombat() is the ONLY way the app writes this object, and it clamps every numeric field on save (see each field's min/max below) so a stray keystroke in Admin can never save an unpayable prize or an unreachable HP value. Some fields below apply only under one combatMode — see each field's own description.

prizeRule.description: Which formula decides the winner's prize (in POINTS) when a house's HP is reduced to zero on Battle Day. Hit points are separate from house points — points are the scoreboard/currency, HP is what a strike removes, and the LOSER NEVER LOSES POINTS no matter which rule is chosen; only the winner's total moves. 'gap' (default): the winner takes half the point gap they were behind by (see 'gapShare') — self-limiting, since the prize shrinks to nothing as the trailing house catches up. Simulated over a 9-week term with houses earning unequally, the best-behaved house still won the term and the point spread narrowed. 'percent': the winner takes a percentage of the DEFENDER's total points (see 'prizePercent') — this compounds hard (simulated prizes grew from 281 to 1671 points across a term) and the WORST-behaved house won the simulated term; it is offered because a teacher may expect this style of rule, not because it is advised. 'flat': every win pays the same fixed number of points (see 'prizeFlat') — predictable and never compounds, but if set below the cost of the cheapest shop weapon, nobody will ever bother attacking.

gapShare.description: Percent of the point gap between attacker and defender awarded to the winner, when prizeRule is 'gap'. Clamped to 0-100 by store.updateCombat().

prizePercent.description: Percent of the defeated house's total points awarded to the winner, when prizeRule is 'percent'. Clamped to 0-100 by store.updateCombat().

prizeFlat.description: Fixed number of points awarded to the winner, when prizeRule is 'flat'. Clamped to 0-9999 by store.updateCombat() — 9999 is MAX_DELTA, the hard ceiling on any single points transaction in the whole app (a guard against a mistyped award, like a stray zero turning a 50-point award into 500,000 — not a game rule). A prize configured above that ceiling could never actually be paid in full, so the setting itself is capped there too.

punchingDown.description: HIT-POINTS MODE ONLY (combatMode 'hp'). Whether a house is allowed to attack another house that currently holds FEWER term points than it does. Off by default: without this guard, the leading house could farm the last-place house every Battle Day, which is the failure mode a classroom would regret most. The duel mode's own punching-down flag is 'duelPunchDown' below — the two are independent so switching combatMode does not silently change the other mode's rule.

duelPunchDown.description: MR. D'S RULES ONLY (combatMode 'duel'). Whether a house may throw an attack (including choosing the Catapult's second target) at a house holding fewer points than itself. Defaults to true — the OPPOSITE default from the hit-points mode's 'punchingDown' above — because Mr. D's own game is played by every core each week and blocking the leader from attacking would take the class in front most often out of Battle Day altogether.

hpBase.description: HIT-POINTS MODE ONLY. Base max HP every house starts a Battle Day cycle with, before any points-based bonus is added. Clamped to 1-10000 by store.updateCombat().

hpPer500.description: HIT-POINTS MODE ONLY. Extra max HP granted per 500 TERM points a house currently holds — maxHp = hpBase + hpPer500 * floor(points / 500), see store.getMaxHp(). A mild brake on everyone piling onto the current point leader every week: the richer a house gets, the tougher it is to finish off in combat. Clamped to 0-10000 by store.updateCombat().

teacherScore.description: The +/- amount on the always-visible 'Teacher scoring' row inside the Battle Day arena (both rule sets) — a manual award/deduction that spends no item and rolls no dice. Used to be hardcoded to 10 in battle.js; now teacher-editable.

sfx.description: Teacher-recorded sound replacements per effect slot (Admin → ⚙️ Settings → Sound). Seeded with real values (the shipped /sfx file paths) by store.js's defaultState() on a brand-new install — it is never null there. A null/missing value only ever turns up in an OLDER SAVED state that predates this setting or one of its slots; store.js load() rebuilds it on every load with EVERY slot below present, each holding either '' (use the built-in synth tone, or — for 'battlecry' — true silence) or a path under /sfx pointing at the teacher's own recording. An unassigned slot never leaves the app silent, except 'battlecry' on purpose: it is a spoken voice line ('It's Battle Day. Attack!'), and a synthesized beep would be worse than nothing, so it just stays quiet until the teacher records one. audio.sfx(name) always tries the teacher's assigned file first and falls back to the built-in WebAudio-synthesized tone only if the slot is blank or the file fails to load/play.

battlecry.description: Battle Day war-cry line, played as the Battle Day cinematic slams in. No synth fallback — blank means silence, not a beep.

sword.description: A strike landing on another house.

thud.description: A shield holding, or points/HP coming off.

coin.description: The reward chime when a house scores. This one fires often.

fanfare.description: Played when a Mythic relic is claimed on a natural 20.

roll.description: The Die of Destiny tumbling. Ships blank on purpose — the built-in synthesized rattle already covers it.

diceland.description: The Die of Destiny settling right after the roll (a short, quiet tap — deliberately its own slot rather than sharing 'thud', which is a much heavier combat sound and used to land out of time with the tumble). Ships blank on purpose — the built-in tap already covers it.

diceProphecy.description: TEACHER OVERRIDES ONLY, keyed by outcome id — NOT the outcome table itself. The Die of Destiny's d20 table (Admin → ⚙️ Settings → Dice prophecy) ships in code, in store.js's defaultDiceProphecy(), and store.js merges these overrides over it at load; a fresh or never-edited install saves {} here. That is the whole point: a wording or points fix in store.js reaches an install that has already saved, because only the fields the teacher actually changed are in this file. Each entry holds ONLY the changed fields out of 'points', 'title', 'desc' and 'emoji' (the four store.saveDiceOutcome accepts) — an outcome put back to its shipped value drops out of the object entirely. 'min'/'max'/'hasButton'/'mythic' can never appear here: they always come from the shipped table, so every one of the 20 faces maps to exactly one outcome with no gaps. LEGACY: an ARRAY here is the pre-override shape (a full copy of the whole table, one object per outcome, written by every version before this one); store.js load() converts it to overrides once — comparing each row against the shipped table and keeping only genuine differences — and the next save writes the object form. The one-time conversion also drops descriptions matching wordings the app itself shipped earlier (RETIRED_DICE_DESCS in store.js), which are the app's words rather than the teacher's. The 'settings.diceDescRev' revision marker that used to drive that correction by hand is deleted on load and never written again.

additionalProperties.description: Only the fields this outcome's teacher edit actually changed; anything omitted keeps the shipped value.

points.description: Points awarded (may be negative, e.g. Catastrophe's -10). Clamped to ±9999 (MAX_DELTA) on save.

title.description: Outcome title on the plaque, trimmed to 40 characters.

backupDownload.description: Master switch for the once-a-school-day safety-net download (see js/core/backup.js's maybeDailyDownload) that saves mrd-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.json to the browser's normal Downloads folder. Absent/missing is treated as true (store.getSettings().backupDownload !== false) — this key is only ever written when the teacher explicitly toggles it off in Admin → ⚙️ Settings → Backup & Restore, so a fresh install has no key at all rather than an explicit true.

awardPresets.description: The teacher's most-used point awards, shown as one-tap buttons on the Records screen (Admin-editable). Seeded with five defaults: Bell Ringer done (+5), Homework Hero (+10), Great teamwork (+5), Map Quiz Champion (+50), and Penalty (-5).

points.description: Points to award when the preset is tapped. May be negative (e.g. the Penalty preset).

tag.description: Transaction tag recorded when this preset is used (see transactions[].tag).

houses.description: Teacher edits to the four built-in houses — name, motto, accent colour, and artwork (Admin → Houses). Keyed by houseId (1-4). Applied IN PLACE over the shipped house defaults at load time (see applyHouseOverrides() in store.js), so every module already holding a reference to a house object sees the new values immediately, including right after a rename — nothing has to re-fetch. An empty object ({}, the default) means no house has been customised; store.resetHouse() removes a house's entry here to revert it to the pristine shipped default.

additionalProperties.description: Only the keys the teacher actually changed need be present; anything omitted keeps the shipped default.

accentSoft.description: RGBA soft-glow colour, auto-derived from 'accent' whenever the teacher changes it — never set independently.

introVideos.description: TEACHER OVERRIDES ONLY — what the teacher has ADDED to, and HIDDEN from, the intro-video presets offered in the POTW (Place of the Week) dropdown. The presets themselves ship in code, in CONFIG.POTW_INTRO_VIDEOS (js/config.js), and store.js merges these overrides over them at load, so dropping a new file into /videos and listing it there makes it appear on every install — including one that has already saved. That is the whole reason this is no longer a copy of the list: it used to be, and when the intros changed from YouTube embeds to local /videos files, saved installs kept offering only the two dead YouTube presets and 'intro-01' resolved to nothing at all. Order: shipped presets first (in CONFIG order), then teacher-added ones. LEGACY: an ARRAY here is the pre-override shape (the whole merged list); store.js load() converts it once, keeping only entries that are not shipped or that differ from the shipped one, and dropping the two withdrawn YouTube preset ids ('rock', 'classic'). The conversion deliberately hides NOTHING, however many shipped presets the old list is missing — an old list predates the current presets, so absence there means 'never seen', not 'deleted'.

added.description: Presets the teacher created in Admin, plus any shipped preset whose label or url they changed (matched by id, and rendered in the shipped preset's place rather than appended).

hidden.description: Ids of shipped presets the teacher deleted in Admin (store.deleteIntroVideo). This is how a deletion is recorded now that the list is not copied: before, the deleted preset was simply missing from the saved copy and the backfill put it straight back on the next load. If every preset is hidden and none added, the shipped list is offered anyway — the dropdown must never be empty.

inventory.description:
What each house currently holds, bought but not yet spent — its armoury. Keyed by houseId (1-4); each value is itemId -> count still held. Read/written by store.getInventory()/addToInventory()/consumeFromInventory(), shared by BOTH Battle Day rule sets (settings.combatMode), which use it very differently, and it is emptied ({}) every time combatMode is switched — an item bought under one rule set means nothing under the other. Cleared entries are removed from the object entirely once their count drops to zero.

Under combatMode 'hp': only shop items whose effect.kind is 'attack', 'steal', or 'pierce' are stockpiled this way (see store.STOCKPILE_KINDS) — buying one banks it here instead of firing it on the spot. Using it (store.consumeFromInventory()) removes one copy and deals damage to the target's top-level 'hp', never touching this object again beyond the removal. Shields, damage-reduction relics ('shield'/'reduce'), and wildcards ('wild') are deliberately NOT stockpiled here — they are timed protection that starts the moment they're bought, or (wildcards) a gamble that resolves immediately at purchase.

Under combatMode 'duel' (Mr. D's rules): EVERY duel item a house owns lives here, including defenses, the Stone of Seeing, the Shroud of Secrecy, the Time Turner and the Bag of Holding — not just attacks. A house may hold at most one 'attack'-slot item and one 'defense'-slot item at a time (two of each if it owns 'bagofholding', which is never itself consumed); 'utility'-slot items (stone/shroud/timeturner/bagofholding) don't count against that limit. An attack item is always consumed when thrown, whether or not it was countered; a defense item is only consumed when it actually blocks something.

additionalProperties.description: itemId -> count of that item currently banked, unused, by this house.
Number of this item currently held. Removed from the object entirely once it drops to zero.

frozen.description: MR. D'S RULES ONLY (settings.combatMode 'duel'). houseId -> epoch ms until which that house cannot earn ANY points from anywhere — the ±/quick-points panel, quests, the Die of Destiny, POTW bounties, all of it — caused by an uncountered Legendary Ice Axe (see the duel shop catalog's 'iceaxe' item). Stored as an EXPIRY, not a countdown, so it survives a reload and needs nothing ticking to stay correct after a weekend with the laptop shut. store.js load() prunes any entry whose expiry has already passed on every load. A house may still be attacked and still lose points normally while frozen; only earning is blocked. Admin → ⚔️ Battle Day → House status & holdings lists every frozen house with an Un-freeze button.

additionalProperties.description: Expiry timestamp in milliseconds; if > Date.now(), the house is frozen and cannot earn points.

shrouded.description: MR. D'S RULES ONLY. houseId -> epoch ms until which a Shroud of Secrecy hides that house's held items from a Stone of Seeing — a Stone spent against a shrouded house is still consumed but reveals nothing. Expiry-based like 'frozen' above, and pruned on every load by store.js. Does NOT block attacks or hide the house from being targeted; it only blinds the Stone of Seeing.

additionalProperties.description: Expiry timestamp in milliseconds; if > Date.now(), a Stone of Seeing used on this house reveals nothing.

revealed.description: MR. D'S RULES ONLY. viewerHouseId -> { targetHouseId: ts } — records which houses have used a Stone of Seeing (or landed a strike, which also reveals) to see which other houses' held items, so the Battle Day screen can keep showing that information face-up for the rest of the session instead of flashing it once. Cleared entirely when Battle Day ends (🏳️ End Battle), so next session's holdings start secret again for everyone.

additionalProperties.description: targetHouseId -> timestamp (ms) the viewer last saw that house's held items.

hp.description: HIT-POINTS MODE ONLY (settings.combatMode 'hp') — cleared to {} the moment combatMode switches to 'duel', since Mr. D's rules deal damage straight to points and have no HP concept at all. houseId -> DAMAGE TAKEN so far in the current Battle Day cycle — this is NOT current hit points, which is a deliberate design choice. Storing 'current HP' looked right until a house won a battle: the prize pushed its point total over a 500-point boundary (see settings.combat.hpPer500), its maximum HP rose as a result, and its untouched 'current' HP suddenly read something like 120/130 — it LOOKED wounded purely for having gotten richer. Storing damage taken instead is invariant to the maximum moving: a house's actual remaining HP is always computed on the fly as store.getMaxHp(houseId) - hp[houseId] (see store.getHp()). Cleared back to {} at the start of every Battle Day session (store.resetAllHp()), so no house arrives already half-beaten from a prior week.

additionalProperties.description: Cumulative HP damage taken by this house since the last Battle Day reset.

quests.description: Class Quests system (one active per core, completion teacher-confirmed). The BOARD itself is not stored here: the shipped quests live in code, in store.js's defaultQuestCatalog(), and this object holds only the teacher's overrides ('edits'/'added'/'deleted', the same pattern as 'shop') plus the two things that are records rather than content — which quest each core is on now, and every completion. Four per-field backfills used to run on load, writing 'repeatable', 'penalty', 'type' and 'icon' into every saved quest as each field was added to the catalog; all four are gone. A field the app can DERIVE is never stored — the give-up penalty is half the reward unless the teacher sets one, and an untyped quest borrows its category's icon — because storing a default turns it into a fact: a quest whose reward was later raised kept a penalty worked out from the old one. store.failQuest(), quests.js and admin.js each already computed the same fallback at the point of use, and that is now the only rule. LEGACY: a save holding a 'catalog' array is the old full-copy shape; store.js load() converts it once, dropping values that merely repeat what the app would derive, and treating a shipped quest missing from it as deleted — the board was copied whole, so absence is the only record a deletion ever left.

edits.description: questId -> the fields of that SHIPPED quest the teacher changed, and nothing else (field shapes are as in 'catalog' below). A quest edited back to its shipped values drops out entirely, and a value equal to one the app would derive is never written.

added.description: Quests the teacher wrote themselves, stored whole — there is no shipped quest to diff them against.

deleted.description: Ids of SHIPPED quests the teacher deleted in Admin (store.deleteQuest). Any house holding one has it cleared at the same moment.

catalog.description: LEGACY ONLY — the old full copy of the whole quest board, and the shape of a quest for every key above. store.js load() converts it to 'edits'/'added'/'deleted' the first time it sees one and never writes this key again; it is still what a backup file exported before that change contains. NOTE that 'penalty', 'repeatable', 'type' and 'icon' may all be ABSENT on a quest now: each is derived where it is used when missing (penalty = half of 'points', repeatable = false, type = 'service', icon = the category's icon), and a value equal to the derived one is deliberately not stored.

type.description: Quest category. Drives filtering on the Quests board and the fallback icon shown on the card when 'icon' is blank. 'service' (Helping the school run) is also the fallback category for anything untyped — a quest the teacher wrote before this field existed, or one restored from an older backup, lands here until they pick a real one. 'academic' = Learning and schoolwork, 'community' = Giving and kindness, 'habit' = Daily and weekly conduct.

icon.description: The emoji shown on this quest's card, so a board of ~20 quests doesn't repeat the same handful of symbols. Blank means 'no icon of its own' — the card falls back to its category's icon instead (see 'type').

repeatable.description: If true, any house may accept this quest again after someone else finishes it (e.g. 'attend a school event'). If false, it is a one-shot: it leaves the board for good once any house completes it.

penalty.description: Points deducted from a house that gives up on this quest after accepting it (store.failQuest() — the quest also returns to the board for another house to take). Defaults to half of 'points' if never explicitly set — abandoning a quest should sting without erasing a week's work. Backfilled by store.js load() for any quest saved before this field existed, so it may be briefly absent on a catalog entry a teacher just created in Admin before their first save round-trips.

example.title: Campus Cleanup Crew
example.desc: Clean a shared school space during recess or lunch. Proof: before & after photos.

active.description: Currently active quest per core: core -> { questId, startedTs }.

questId.description: ID of the active quest for this core.

startedTs.description: Timestamp when students accepted the quest (Date.now()).

title.description: Quest title at time of completion.

shop.description: TEACHER OVERRIDES ONLY — what the teacher has changed about the Magic Shop (Admin → 🔮 Shop). Neither catalog is stored here. There are TWO catalogs, one per settings.combatMode ('duel' = Mr. D's rules, 'hp' = hit points, see COMBAT_MODES in store.js), both ship in code (defaultDuelCatalog() / defaultHpCatalog()), and store.js merges these overrides over the shipped list at load — the active mode's into 'catalog' and the other mode's into 'parked', in memory only. THE TWO CATALOGS ARE INDEPENDENT ID NAMESPACES and every key below is split by mode for exactly that reason: 'catapult' and 'cloak' each name a completely different item in the two, and the old by-id migrations each needed a hand-written scope note to avoid rewriting one with the other. Because the shipped items are read from code on every load, a price rebalance, a wording fix, a new piece of artwork or a brand-new item reaches an install that has already saved — which is what the three one-time patches this replaced (a 'seeded' id list, 'descRev' and 'artRev') each existed to do once, by hand. LEGACY: a save holding 'catalog'/'parked'/'seeded' is the old full-copy shape; store.js load() converts it once (per mode, using that mode's 'seeded' list to tell a deliberate deletion from an item shipped since), backfills shipped artwork into any item that has no image at all — the last thing 'artRev' was for — and the next save writes the shape below. 'descRev'/'artRev' are dropped and never written again.

edits.description: Per-mode, per-id diffs against the SHIPPED item: only the fields the teacher actually changed in Admin's shop editor. An item edited back to its shipped values drops out entirely.

added.description: Items the teacher created themselves, per mode, stored whole — there is no shipped item to diff them against. An id here that later becomes a shipped id is ignored in favour of the shipped item, so the same id can never appear twice in one catalog.

deleted.description: Ids of SHIPPED items the teacher deleted in Admin, per mode. This is how a deletion is recorded now that the catalog is not copied: before, the item was simply missing from the saved copy and a separate 'seeded' id list existed to stop the next load putting it straight back.

events.description: All calendar events for the term.

endDate.description: Event end date (YYYY-MM-DD), optional for multi-day events.

core.description: Which core(s) this event applies to.

transactions.description: Immutable log of all point changes (additions/deductions).

ts.description: Timestamp in milliseconds (Date.now() at time of transaction).

houseId.description: Which house earned or lost points.

delta.description: Points added (positive) or deducted (negative). Clamped to ±9999.

reason.description: Human-readable description (e.g., 'Correct bell ringer answer', 'Bought: Aegis Shield').

tag.description: Machine-readable category for filtering and for the ledger analytics breakdown (store.getBreakdown()). Real values written by the app today: 'manual' (a teacher tap — award presets, quick adjust with a custom reason, house-wide awards), 'attack' (points looted by a 'steal' shop item, or the legacy direct-points store.applyAttack() path used by teacher-scoring corrections), 'battle' (a Battle Day victory prize), 'dice' (Die of Destiny roll outcome), 'potw' (Place of the Week quiz bounty payout), 'quest' (quest completed or abandoned), 'shop' (a purchase deducting its cost), 'wild' (a wildcard shop item's random points swing), 'quick' (the Quick Adjust control in the top bar, when no custom reason is given). '' is the function default (store.addPoints) for a transaction created without an explicit tag; it should be rare/legacy in practice. Older/unused values that used to appear here ('challenge', 'daily', 'event') have been dropped — nothing in the codebase writes them any more.

shields.description: houseId -> expiry epoch (milliseconds) for a FULL-BLOCK shield (e.g. Phalanx Formation, Aegis Shield, Moat & Drawbridge, The Great Wall) — this is the legacy/original defensive item, kept as its own top-level key for backward compatibility rather than folded into 'defenses' below. While active, it blocks an incoming attack outright UNLESS the attack is a 'pierce' item, which ignores it entirely (see store.applyAttack / the Battle Day HP-combat resolver). Duration varies per item (12-48 hours depending on which shield was bought), not a fixed 24h. Expired entries are pruned by store.js load() on every load, so an old backup can never revive a shield that should have run out.

additionalProperties.description: Expiry timestamp in milliseconds; if > Date.now(), the shield is active.

defenses.description: houseId -> { reduce: expiry epoch ms }. Damage-HALVING relics — distinct from the full-block 'shields' above. These come from the Mythic-only shop items (Spy Network, Lookout Tower, Oracle of Delphi), granted only when a house rolls a natural 20 on the Die of Destiny, and are never purchasable directly. While active, any non-piercing hit against this house is halved rather than blocked outright (see store.hasReduction() / store.applyAttack()); a 'pierce' item ignores this too, exactly like a full shield. Expired entries are pruned by store.js load() on every load, mirroring the 'shields' cleanup.

additionalProperties.description: Currently only ever holds a 'reduce' key, but is an object (not a bare number) so future defensive relic types can add sibling keys without a breaking migration.

reduce.description: Expiry timestamp in milliseconds; if > Date.now(), incoming non-piercing damage against this house is halved.

itineraries.description: Daily schedule for each core (1–4), displayed on the Morning Dashboard.

potwBounties.description: Ledger of paid Place-of-the-Week quiz bounties, so relaunching the same voyage (e.g. after a page reload mid-week, or a teacher re-opening the same destination) can never pay the same bounty twice. Keyed by '<profileKey>|<weekOf>|<questionIndex>' (see store.bountyKey()) rather than just the question index alone, so the SAME question number in a profile that gets re-scheduled to a different week is treated as a brand-new, unpaid bounty.

houseId.description: Which house was paid this bounty.

potw.description: Place of the Week voyages (cinematic geography lessons with 3D maps).

active.description: Key of the currently-active POTW destination (e.g., 'mesopotamia').

profiles.description: Collection of POTW destinations. Added/edited in Admin → 🌍 Place of the Week.

shopEdits.description: itemId -> the fields of that SHIPPED item the teacher changed, and nothing else. Values follow the same shapes as 'shopItem' below. One extra key can appear: '__unset', an array naming shipped fields the teacher's version does not have AT ALL — Admin's shop editor rebuilds an item field by field, so clearing every counter off the Sword of Destiny leaves it with no 'counteredBy' key, and without this the shipped item merging back over it would quietly restore the counter they just removed.

__unset.description: Shipped fields this item no longer has at all.

net.desc: My own words about the net.

shopItem.description: One Magic Shop item. Shape overlaps between the two combat modes (id/name/emoji/image/cost/desc/effect are common to both) but 'slot'/'counteredBy'/'blocks' apply ONLY to the duel ('duel' combatMode) catalog, and 'mythicOnly' applies only to the hit-points ('hp') catalog — Mr. D's rules ship no mythic-only items out of the box, though a teacher could still flag one.

id.description: Unique item ID within its catalog (auto-generated or teacher-set). The 'duel' and 'hp' catalogs are independent id namespaces — 'catapult' and 'cloak' each name a completely different item in the two catalogs; nothing ever merges them.

image.description: Item artwork: a static repo path under images/shop/ (every shipped duel item ships one, like the house shields — no upload needed), a 'media:…' IndexedDB key from an Admin upload (which always wins over a shipped path), or '' for emoji-only.

cost.description: TERM points required to purchase. Forced to 0 for 'mythicOnly' items (hit-points catalog) — they cannot be bought at all, only granted.

desc.description: Item description and effect summary shown on its shop card. Clamped to roughly 3 lines on the card; longer text is silently cut off.

mythicOnly.description: HIT-POINTS CATALOG. If true, this item can never be purchased in the Magic Shop (its cost is forced to 0) — it is granted automatically as a Mythic Triumph reward when a house rolls a natural 20 on the Die of Destiny (store.getMythicRewards()/grantMythicItem()). The three shipped mythic items (Spy Network, Lookout Tower, Oracle of Delphi) are all 'reduce' kind. The shipped duel catalog has none of these; a natural 20 under Mr. D's rules simply awards its points with no relic unless the teacher adds a mythicOnly duel item themselves.

slot.description: DUEL CATALOG ONLY. A house may hold at most one 'attack' item and one 'defense' item at a time (two of each if it owns the Bag of Holding, a 'utility' item); 'utility' items never count against that limit. See the top-level 'inventory' key.

counteredBy.description: DUEL CATALOG, attack items. Ids of the 'defense'-slot items that cancel this attack outright when the defender is holding one at the moment it lands. Empty array (e.g. The Catapult) means nothing in the shop counters it.

blocks.description: DUEL CATALOG, defense items. Ids of the 'attack'-slot items this defense stops. The inverse of 'counteredBy' on the matching attack item(s).

effect.description: What the item does when used. The 'kind' enum spans BOTH catalogs — a kind from one mode never appears in the other's shipped items, though nothing stops a teacher typing one in Admin.

kind.description:
HIT-POINTS CATALOG — 'attack': stockpiled (top-level 'inventory'); struck on Battle Day it removes 'amount' HIT POINTS from a chosen house. 'steal': stockpiled, same HP-damage mechanic, but the target is always whichever house currently leads; the attacker additionally gains POINTS equal to the HP damage that actually landed. 'pierce': stockpiled, like 'attack' but ignores shields AND damage-reduction. 'shield': NOT stockpiled — buying it immediately blocks incoming attacks for 'amount' hours. 'reduce': NOT stockpiled — immediately halves incoming non-piercing damage for 'amount' hours. 'wild': NOT stockpiled — resolves immediately at purchase as a random points swing of up to ±'amount'.

DUEL CATALOG (Mr. D's rules) — 'damage': on a Battle Day throw (see the duel flow), if not countered by the defender's held item, the app rolls 'dice' on screen, multiplies by 'mult', and removes that many POINTS (never HP) from the target, floored at 0 (it can never go negative). 'steal': identical roll/counter mechanic, but whatever amount actually lands is ALSO credited to the attacker's points ('anonymous' true suppresses the attacker's name on the victim's ledger line only — everything else about the throw still names them). 'freeze': rolls 'dice' (no 'mult') for a number of SCHOOL days the target house cannot earn any points at all from anywhere; ends early via Admin → ⚔️ Battle Day → House status & holdings. 'block': a defense-slot item with no roll of its own — see the matching attack's 'counteredBy'. 'reveal' (Stone of Seeing): turns another chosen house's held items face-up on screen for the rest of that Battle Day session; consumed even if it reveals nothing (the target is shrouded). 'hide' (Shroud of Secrecy): makes this house's held items unreadable to a Stone of Seeing for one week (see top-level 'shrouded'). 'timeturn' (Time Turner): deletes the log entries for the most recent strike that hit this house, as though it never happened, and lifts a freeze if that was the strike undone. 'extraslot' (Bag of Holding): never consumed; permanently raises this house's attack/defense holding limit from one to two.

amount.description: HIT-POINTS CATALOG. Effect magnitude: hit points removed (attack/steal/pierce), hours of protection (shield/reduce), or the ceiling on a wildcard's random ± point swing. Not used by duel-catalog items, which use 'dice'/'mult' instead.

dice.description: DUEL CATALOG. Dice notation rolled on screen for this effect, e.g. '2d6', '1d6', '3d6'. Used by 'damage', 'steal' and 'freeze' kinds.

mult.description: DUEL CATALOG, 'damage'/'steal' only. The roll total is multiplied by this before being applied to points — e.g. 2d6 × 100. Not used by 'freeze', which applies the raw roll as a day count.

targets.description: DUEL CATALOG. Number of houses this attack strikes with a single roll. Only The Catapult ships with 2 — the app asks who the second target is before anything is spent, and the same single roll is applied to both houses in turn.

anonymous.description: DUEL CATALOG, 'steal' only. If true (only the Cloak of Invisibility ships this way), the victim's own ledger line omits the attacker's name. Nothing else about the throw is hidden — the Battle Day screen and the attacker's own ledger line still name them.
